claims.claim: The file 'bin/jpower.bin' (the community-extracted jpower table, 311 entries of 304 bytes matching JPowerEntry.BlockSize) is opened by a function at 0x021652E8 in the ov5 overlay (the Jump Galaxy / deck-builder menu overlay), whose own debug-allocator tag strings identify it as 'JPowerData_Create' (string at 0x021713D8, source tag 'JPowerData.cpp' at 0x021713EC). The function allocates an 8-byte wrapper object (size #8 at 0x021652F4), then loads r0 from a PC-relative literal that resolves to the string table entry 0x0216536C=0x021713FC ('bin/jpower.bin'), and passes it as the first argument to the generic file-open call 0x2033410 with r1=0, r2=0. The loaded file handle (r4) is then queried via its own vtable (call through [[r4]+4]->+0x2c) to obtain a raw data pointer, which is stored into the wrapper object's second word (object+4) at 0x02165358.
open_questions: xrefs-to 0x021713FC (the 'bin/jpower.bin' string) found exactly ONE reference in the whole ROM (this ov5 site). Since ov5 (JGalaxy/deck-builder) and ov6 (battle) cannot be resident simultaneously (both share the 0x0214CD20 overlay window), does the real-time battle engine (ov6) read jpower data from this same loaded blob via a cached global pointer, or does it obtain per-attack damage data through an entirely different path (e.g. the arm9 per-character asset loader at 0x02074728) that never opens this file directly? This is now the single highest-value next question: if ov6 never touches this blob, 'jpower.bin' may be a MENU-ONLY display table (e.g. for a Jump-Power stat/graph shown in Jump Galaxy screens), not the live combat table, despite the byte-level match to the researcher-labelled jpower.bin file.

claims.claim: The per-entry stride used to index into the loaded jpower.bin blob is confirmed by code to be exactly 0x130 (304) bytes, matching JPowerEntry.BlockSize from the toolkit's own binary format reader (Binary2JPower.cs). The accessor function at 0x02165398 (ov5) takes the wrapper object from the previous claim as r0 and an integer index as r1, computes r2 = r1 * 0x130, and returns the raw entry pointer via [[r0+4] + r2] -- i.e. entryPtr = basePtr[index * 304]. A sibling accessor at 0x021653AC additionally adds two more index terms (r2*0x3c and r3*0x14) on top of the same base+r1*0x130 address, suggesting a nested sub-structure within each 304-byte block whose purpose (a 60-byte middle stride and a 20-byte inner stride, the latter numerically identical to CollisionEntry.EntrySize) was not resolved this round. This accessor is called from at least 9 call sites, all inside ov5 (confirmed via xrefs-to on both 0x02165398 and 0x021653AC).
open_questions: The index passed at 0x021626EC is read from [wrapperObj+0x104], which was set at construction time (0x021624C4: str r4,[r8,#0x104]) directly from that object's first constructor parameter, with no visible '& 0xFF' masking. Is this parameter a raw jpower entry ID (0-310), a classId needing the documented 'classId & 0xFF' block-selection (see jpower-Mapping.md), or an unrelated menu-cursor index? Not resolved this round.

claims.claim: An exhaustive check of every one of the 324 branch (bl/blx) call sites to the generic long-division subroutine 0x0200D12C ROM-wide (arm9 + all 14 overlays, enumerated via xrefs-to) found exactly 6 sites where the instruction immediately preceding the call sets the divisor to literal 5 (mov r1,#5, opcode 0510a0e3): one in arm9 and five in the ov5 overlay (covered in the next claim). This arm9 site (0x020795E8, inside function 0x020790F0) is unrelated to combat/jpower: it computes two back-to-back /5 divisions on register sl/fp, each result immediately scaled by x3 (add r0,r0,r0,lsl#1) and left-shifted into a fixed-point stack slot, matching UI icon-grid layout math (row/column pixel-position computation), not damage. It does not reference the character (char+0x56c / char+0x1a8 / char+0x1b4) or jpower structures identified in the damage-pipeline round-1 findings.
open_questions: If the runtime damage /5 exists as literal integer division at all, it must use a divisor register set more than 2 instructions before the bl (not checked by this sweep), a small-range approximate reciprocal multiply with a non-canonical constant (e.g. x*51>>8), a Thumb-mode call site (this sweep assumed 4-byte ARM instructions immediately preceding each call; a Thumb caller would be misread by the fixed -8-byte lookback), or is not implemented as a runtime division at all (e.g. the /5 term is baked into data offline, or realized via a small lookup table not detectable via search-imm/pool-values).

claims.claim: Of the same ROM-wide sweep of 324 call sites to 0x0200D12C (previous claim), the remaining 5 literal-divisor-5 sites are all inside the ov5 overlay (0x021535C0, 0x02159D24, 0x02159D38, 0x02159EC0, 0x0215A014) and are likewise unrelated to combat/jpower: each splits a value (from [object+0x124], or a plain register) into quotient and remainder via two consecutive divide-by-5 calls, the standard idiom for converting a 1-D list index into row/column coordinates of a 5-column menu grid (e.g. at 0x021535C8 the quotient is combined via mla with a row-width constant and the remainder is added as a x4 column offset). None reference the character/jpower structures from the damage-pipeline round-1 findings. Combined with the previous claim (the one arm9 site) and round1's claim that the canonical /5 magic-multiply constants (0x66666667 / 0xCCCCCCCD) also appear nowhere near damage code, this rules out BOTH canonical ARM division idioms (inlined magic-multiply and generic-subroutine-with-literal-divisor) as the implementation of the confirmed damage formula's floor(damage1/5) term, anywhere in the ROM.
open_questions: Same caveats as the arm9 site: this sweep cannot rule out a Thumb-mode call site, a divisor register set further back than 2 instructions, or a non-canonical small-range reciprocal-multiply approximation.

claims.claim: The per-hit HP-delta values read at scratch offsets +0xe8/+0x130 (round1 claims 7-8, function 0x02158B20) belong to a sub-object reached via a two-level pointer chain rooted on the character struct: char+0x1a8 points to a freshly-allocated 0x1f0-byte (496-byte) 'MoveInfo' object (allocated at 0x02156A58 inside function 0x02156A38, which is invoked when an attack/move starts), and that MoveInfo object's own +0x10 field is a pointer to a second sub-object whose +0x40 field is a flags word (bit 0x800 gates whether the +0xe8/+0x130 deltas get applied) and whose +0xe8/+0x130 fields are the two already-computed HP-like deltas. The char+0x1a8 field itself is written by a small setter function at 0x021570EC (str r0,[r4,#0x1a8], called with r0=the MoveInfo object). This narrows down the object's identity and allocation site (previously unknown in round1) but the exact call/function that WRITES the sub-object's +0xe8 field was not located this round: an exhaustive search-imm scan for immediate offset 0xe8 across the whole ROM (135 hits) found no other write site whose base register chain matches [[char+0x1a8]+0x10], consistent with round1's independent finding of the same gap.
claims.gdb_check: break 0x02156A58; log the size argument (r0=#0x1f0) and record the returned pointer, then break 0x021570F4 and confirm r0 (the value stored into char+0x1a8) equals that same pointer, confirming the MoveInfo object's lifecycle; then break 0x02158BA8 and single-step backward (or set a hardware watchpoint on [r1+0xe8]) during a real hit to find the actual instruction that last wrote it, which this static pass could not locate.
open_questions: Who writes the sub-object's +0xe8 and +0x130 fields, and does that writer perform the /5 + (tier-2) + x1.5 computation, or does it just copy an already-fully-resolved delta produced elsewhere (e.g. by the indirect jpower lookup itself)?

suggested_next_angles: Resolve the open question in claim 1: determine whether ov6 (battle) ever opens/references the same jpower.bin blob loaded by ov5's JPowerData_Create, e.g. by checking whether the arm9 per-character asset loader (0x02074728, which fetches ~24 per-character sub-resources by numeric ID via 0x2074c48/0x2035e88) has any fetch whose ID range or resulting pointer gets used with the same 0x130-byte stride confirmed in claim 2 -- no such usage was found in this round's (limited) look at that function.

If ov6 truly never touches jpower.bin directly, pivot the 'indirect resolution' question: the real per-hit damage magnitude may be computed from data already resident in the character/collision structures loaded by 0x02074728 (per-character, at classId-derived offsets like char+0x88/+0x8c, or the 16- and 8-entry pointer arrays at char+0x14.. and char+0x5c..) rather than from a live jpower.bin lookup at all -- i.e. jpower.bin's 311 attack templates may be consumed by an OFFLINE/build-time step (or purely by the ov5 menu) rather than by the runtime battle engine.
Re-run the div5 sweep (claim 3) with Thumb-mode-aware lookback (currently ARM-only, fixed -8 bytes) in case the real damage /5 call site is in a Thumb-compiled function.

Investigate the ov3 'JArenaGetJPower'/'JAGetJPower_Add' debug tag strings (0x0215EB14/0x0215EB24) found near collision-pointer-table (0x020924B0) consumers in ov3 (e.g. 0x0215A2D4-0x0215A448) -- static tracing this round found that particular ov3 function building name/label strings (via 0x2074000/0x20741bc) rather than resolving jpower entries, but the 'Arena'-named tag strings and the 0x020924B0 8-byte-stride table warrant a closer follow-up pass, since ov3 appears to be a pre-battle 'Arena setup' overlay distinct from both ov5 (menu) and ov6 (live battle).

The sibling accessor 0x021653AC's extra r2*0x3c + r3*0x14 indexing (claim 2) inside each 304-byte jpower block was not explained; mapping what r2/r3 select could reveal how extendedData or multi-hit/nextId chains are organized in-memory.
